page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 62.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.88 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA T4 GPU from the Turing architecture family, which includes 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, relying instead on network-attached storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights a clear contrast between single-core CPU performance and GPU-driven workloads. Single-core metrics are weak, with Geekbench single-core scoring 937.0 and stress-ng single-core performance falling into the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression is poor at 19.33 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5951.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 13056.17. The integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for prompt processing, achieving 8410.67 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM and 1141.42 tokens/sec on a medium 7B LLM. Text generation on the 7B model is strong at 34.57 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of newer-generation accelerators. The tradeoff involves lower CPU single-core speeds and a lack of local storage, which may bottleneck disk-heavy operations. This instance is suited for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, image processing, and ray tracing workloads that leverage GPU acceleration, while general-purpose multi-threaded tasks like database operations and web serving run with average efficiency.
